hints: Write the division identity $x^2=q(1+4x^2)+r$, where the quotient and remainder are constants.
Compare the $x^2$ coefficients first to determine $q$.
Compare constant terms to determine $r$, then verify the identity exactly.
walkthrough:
Express $x^2$ in terms of the divisor $(1 + 4x^2)$ by matching the leading coefficient:
$$x^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}(4x^2) = \dfrac{1}{4}(4x^2 + 1 - 1) = \dfrac{1}{4}(4x^2 + 1) - \dfrac{1}{4}$$

State the resulting quotient and remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = \dfrac{1}{4}, \quad \text{Remainder} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$$

hints: Use $du=\frac{2}{1+4x^2}\,dx$; the remaining rational integral contains $x^2/(1+4x^2)$.
Replace that quotient using part (a), then integrate the constant and $1/(1+4x^2)$ terms.
Apply both bounds $0$ and $1/2$, use $\tan^{-1}(1)=\pi/4$, and keep the value exact.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts $\int u\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int v\dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u = \tan^{-1}(2x) \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2}{1 + (2x)^2} = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^2}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = x \implies v = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$$

Substitute into the parts formula:
$$\int x\tan^{-1}(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}(2x) - \int \left(\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}(2x) - \int \dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Use the algebraic division from part (a) $\dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4(1 + 4x^2)}$ to evaluate the second integral:
$$\int \dfrac{x^2}{1 + 4x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4(1 + 4x^2)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$\text{Since } \int \dfrac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2x):$$
$$= \dfrac{1}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2x)\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}x - \dfrac{1}{8}\tan^{-1}(2x)$$

Evaluate between the definite limits $x = 0$ and $x = 0.5 = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$\text{Upper limit } x = \dfrac{1}{2}: \quad \tan^{-1}\left(2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \tan^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$$
$$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{8}$$
$$\text{Lower limit } x = 0: \quad \left(0 + \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\tan^{-1}(0) - 0 = 0$$

Subtract the lower limit to find the exact value:
$$\int_0^{0.5} x\tan^{-1}(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{8}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{8}$$
